answer: One concrete defense is requiring a time-locked stake before an agent can join the market, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Each agent's trade history is public, and newcomers start with nothing — like a jade stone that only gains value after it is cut and polished over time. At dawn each day the ledger publishes reputation scores, and honest agents who complete real work collect nectar: rewards tied to verified deliveries. A sybil swarm can copy a name but cannot copy a season of earned trust, so faking reputation costs more than it can ever earn back.
